headline: South Asia: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO.
- Asia: Ukraine believes Russia shared jet-drone technology with North Korea, says Zelensky.
- Africa: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.

Full breakdown follows.

The Caribbean - bottom line: ‘UNINFORMED’ - Global Afrikan Congress rebukes Warmington over slave trade remarks, urges him to do research and apologise.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: ‘UNINFORMED’ - Global Afrikan Congress rebukes Warmington over slave trade remarks, urges him to do research and apologise.
The Global Afrikan Congress (GAC) is demanding an apology from parliamentarian Everald Warmington for his “uninformed assertions” that Black Africans who sold people into the transatlantic slave trade should be held more accountable than Europeans buyers. In an open letter to Warmington, the GAC – an international Pan-African organisation of people of African descent across 35 countries – also urged the St Catherine South Western member of parliament (MP) to undertake necessary research to correct his “colonial miseducation”.

- AllAfrica - Conflict, one hour ago: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.
[Dabanga] Dilling, South Kordofan -- Four civilians, including a child and a woman, have been killed in RSF drone strikes on residential neighbourhoods in Dilling, South Kordofan, the Sudan Doctors Network says. The network condemns the attacks as a grave violation of international humanitarian law.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 6 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan War - Fighting On Ethiopian Border, Drone Attacks On Ed Damazin.
[Dabanga] Ed Damazin -- The RSF-aligned Tasees Alliance forces announced on Saturday that they had taken full control of areas in Roseires locality, north-east of Ed Damazin, capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state, after seizing several areas, including Menze, Jabal El Nimr, Jabal El Num, Basharkat, Matanguya, Mangaling El Jawani, Masnabiga, and Makala.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 19 hours ago: Sudan: 'Drone Strike On El Obeid Shelter Kills Boy, Wounds 12 Children'.
[Dabanga] El Obeid -- A drone strike on a shelter for internally displaced people in El Obeid, North Kordofan, late on Thursday reportedly killed a boy and wounded 12 children, as another drone strike on a university dormitory in the city killed five civilians and injured 47 others.

[RFI] Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut diplomatic ties as a new rebel offensive grips northern Ethiopia, putting two countries that fought together during the last Tigray war on opposing sides. Ethiopia accuses its neighbour of supporting a new anti-government alliance.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO.
A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement will be held on Monday in Riyadh and will focus on regional developments and ongoing cooperation among the member states, the Foreign Office (FO) confirmed. In a statement on social media platform X, the FO said Pakistan’s delegation to the meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) will include Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Haunted by grief, Gaza’s displaced still wait overseas for return.
CAIRO: Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return. Hassayna is one of more than 100,000 Gazans who left the enclave during the war and remain stranded overseas, according to Palestinian Authority figures. They still mourn dead relatives and their destroyed homes and neighbourhoods.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Only ‘just, fair’ talks can end war, Iran tells US.
TEHRAN: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Sunday that there was no military solution to the US’ war against the Islamic Republic and that only negotiations based on “justice and fairness” could end the conflict, as talks between Washington and Tehran appeared to be at an impasse. “If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Araghchi told a gathering of foreign ambassadors in Tehran.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 18 hours ago: PTI terms access to Imran 'principal point of deadlock', claims Centre refused to include it in agreement.
The PTI on Sunday asserted that the main reason for the breakdown of its talks with the Centre was that the latter refused to incorporate terms regarding access to incarcerated party founder Imran Khan into a proposed agreement. Hours-long negotiations yesterday between an opposition delegation comprising the PTI and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), and a joint team of the government and PPP, ended in a deadlock.

North Korea, which has been fortifying its border with South Korea since April 2024, deployed up to 7,000 workers to install mines and fences this year, with some 50 incidents of ‌crossing the border, according to a briefing on Monday by the South’s military. A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure. Built to hunt tanks and support ground troops, the People’s Liberation Army’s main attack helicopter is increasingly being prepared for operations at sea. Crews of the Z-10 are training to fly from ships – a shift that could give Beijing extra firepower in an amphibious assault on Taiwan. India - bottom line: 3 years after Oct 7, Israel honours officer whose Hamas attack warning was ignored.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: 3 years after Oct 7, Israel honours officer whose Hamas attack warning was ignored.
An intelligence officer from Israel's Unit 8200 has been acknowledged for issuing multiple warnings regarding the Hamas invasion prior to the catastrophic attack on October 7, 2023. Unfortunately, those alerts went unheeded, which led to a coordinated assault from Gaza, resulting in heavy casualties and numerous hostages. This incident has led to a critical examination of the systemic shortcomings within Israel's military intelligence operations.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 14 hours ago: 1 dead as Russian drones hit desi pharma plant in Ukraine.
In Ukraine's Sumy region, six Russian drones attacked the Kusum Group's pharmaceutical plant, killing one engineer and injuring others. The main structure of the facility was largely destroyed during the targeted strike, which occurs amid a pattern of similar attacks. The company estimates damage from this incident could exceed $50 million, impacting operations significantly.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Watch: US strike on vessel kills 4 'narco terrorists' in Caribbean.
On Sunday, the US military executed a strike on a go-fast vessel in the Caribbean Sea. This operation resulted in the deaths of four individuals labeled as 'narco-terrorists'. The US Southern Command stated that the vessel was involved in narco-trafficking activities. Since September 2025, the US has intensified strikes on such vessels over narcotics smuggling allegations. Various human rights organizations have condemned these strikes as unlawful extrajudicial killings.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Saudi oil under fire, Aramco plots new routes to keep barrels flowing.
Saudi Aramco is actively developing additional oil export routes and studying overseas storage to address vulnerabilities. The ongoing attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure by Yemen’s Houthi rebels have heightened security concerns. CEO Amin Nasser indicated that crude supply could reach 12 million barrels per day if needed. Physical oil market prices are already experiencing significant premiums due to these disruptions.
